source.passage: They accounted for just 26% of U.S. AI hires in 2025, compared with 50% of hires into non-AI occupations. The gap grows at the top: across 27 countries, women hold only 13% of C-suite AI leadership roles at AI companies.

sources.limitations: LinkedIn platform data. Hiring and leadership are separate populations; figures describe representation, not individual ability or reasons for each hiring outcome.

source.passage: When AI users at work were asked how much they used AI in the last week, 30% of male workers said they used it every day, compared with 17% of female workers. Half of female workers said they used it at least one day, but not every day, and 41% of male workers said the same.
source.additionalPassage: About 55% of U.S. workers said they have used Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the job for at least one of 11 tasks asked about on the U.S. Census Bureau’s March 2026 Household Trends and Outlook Pulse Survey (HTOPS).

sources.limitations: Self-reported usage frequency among AI users at work; not ability, motivation, equal access, usefulness or causes. Official CDN resolves; original www URL returns404.
